newsitem.title: UK: Millwall down on return from suspension.
newsitem.headline: Millwall down on return from suspension.

text.p: Shares in London soccer club Millwall Plc fell sharply on Monday as they returned to the market following a five-month suspension, during which a capital restructuring was agreed.
Millwall shares, suspended in January at 4p, stood at 1-1/4p by 1015 GMT in a volume of over 28 million shares, making it the most active issue in the London market.
Millwall shares were suspended after the management called in administrators when the company was unable to pay interest on its 10 million stg debts.
Millwall has since implemented a capital reconstruction via a share consolidation which effectively halved the number of shares in issue.
Two ordinary shares were consolidated into one share of two pence and then subdivided into one ordinary share and one deferred share of one penny.
In addition, the company issued over 640 million new shares via a placing and over 359 million in a two-for-one rights issue, raising about 6.4 million stg and 3.6 million stg gross respectively.
Some dealers said the stock was underpinned at current levels. "We expect the stock to go better as people perceive the company being run as a business and not just a soccer club," said one.
The company has restructured its board. Earlier this month appointed Theo Paphitis, chairman of stationery group Rymans, as the new chairman.
In April, Paphitis said the company intended to use its New Den stadium to host a number of other events such as concerts to increase revenue.
